dataset_family: Tongji Hospital (Tongji University School of Medicine) Department of Neurology / Memory Clinic, Shanghai; single-site local cohort recruited Jan 2018 - Dec 2021 (43 HC / 46 MCI / 43 AD, 64-channel eyes-closed rsEEG)
method_family: Resting-state EEG within-region phase-amplitude cross-frequency coupling (Tort modulation index on 10 band pairs, global and 8-region averages) with Welch relative band power as a preliminary check; group tests only (Kruskal-Wallis with FDR over regions, DSCF post hoc); no classifier
what_it_shows: In one sample, relative band power differs only for AD (theta up, gamma down versus both HC and MCI) and no HC-vs-MCI power difference is reported; the authors' discussion states an 'absence of abnormal power in MCI patients'. Global-level PAC also shows no HC-vs-MCI difference. Only region-level PAC separates MCI from HC, in 4 region-by-band cells (right temporal and right parietal delta-gamma p=0.022/0.005, theta-gamma p=0.049/0.029, DSCF post hoc after FDR-corrected Kruskal-Wallis). No classification was done.
why: Partly, and only if within-region phase-amplitude coupling is counted as a 'connectivity' measure. The part it shows: in one sample, band power did not separate HC from MCI, while a coupling measure did separate them at the regional level. What it does not show: (1) the measure is within-region PAC (the authors say 'our study only measured CFC in the same brain areas', p.15). It is not inter-regional connectivity, a graph or network metric, or a signal-complexity measure. If the class is read strictly as the statement's 'network, connectivity and complexity measures', the verdict is 'no'. (2) The two measures were not compared like for like. At matched spatial scale (whole head), coupling also failed for HC vs MCI (p.7). Band power was never analysed region by region; it was run only as a prerequisite check for interpreting CFC (p.5-7), and the methods do not name its statistical test. The contrast is therefore whole-head power against region-level coupling, where 8 regions x 10 pairs were tested. (3) The HC-MCI power null is inferred from what the results omit plus one discussion sentence; no HC-MCI power statistic is printed. (4) 'Outperform for discrimination' rests on significant versus non-significant group tests; the authors state that no classification was performed (p.15). (5) MCI was clinical only, with no amyloid or tau confirmation (p.12). Minor: in Table 2 the MCI-AD and HC-AD columns appear swapped relative to the text (e.g. delta-alpha: text AD>HC p<0.001 and AD>MCI p=0.030; table MCI-AD <0.001 and HC-AD 0.030). The HC-MCI column is non-significant throughout, consistent with the text. Independence: a single Shanghai site with no site, cohort or author overlap with P-553 (Hanyang, Korea), P-501 (Wayne State/MADRC), P-463 (Hokuto/Kumagaya, Japan) or P-480 (PREVIEW, Florence). The candidates share no authors. It shares a funding grant number (STI2030 / MOST 2022ZD0211600) with candidate P-1322 (Shenzhen), which is shared funding, not a shared sample. Not in registry_duplicates.json. PDF title, authors and DOI match the block.
